2. This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "MV Act") for the enhancement of the compensation amount awarded in Claim Case No.2156/2018 passed by the Member 20th, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) on 13/09/2023, whereby an amount of Rs.2,21,932/- has been awarded to Dinesh vs Suresh on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164994647/
1 the appellant towards the compensation.

3. The relevant and necessary facts of the case are that on 04/05/2018 at about 12:45 am appellant was going from Ghata Billod to Kheda by Dumper Bearing Registration no. MP-11-H-0680 with his friend Dinesh.
Appellant was Cleaner in the said Dumper.
Driver of Dumper drive the vehicle rashly and negligently and turned turtle the vehicle as a result of which in accident appellant received grievous injuries.
Appellant sustained fracture in left shoulder in clavicle bone and also injury in spleen.
Appellant was hospitalized in Medi Square Hospital form 04/05/2018 to 07/05/2018.
Due to the injuries appellant sustained 8% permanent disablement.
At the time accident,the appellant was working as a cleaner and was getting salary of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries he cannot perform his duties.
4. The appellant preferred a claim petition before the below Tribunal for getting compensation.
The below Tribunal after framing the issues, recording and appreciating the evidence available on record, partly allowed the claim petition and passed an award of Rs.2,21,932/-.
Tribunal exonerated the Insurance Company form the liability.
Being aggrieved by the findings given by the below Tribunal, this appeal has been preferred by the appellant.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that at the time of accident, he was working as a Cleaner and was getting salary of Rs.15,000/- per month, but the below Tribunal has wrongly taken the income as Rs.6,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has erroneously did not awarded any amount towards loss of income and other damages.
No amount has been awarded for the future treatment.

Hence, the claim amount be enhanced appropriately.
6.

From perusal of the award, it appears that although the appellant has claimed that he has sustained permanent disability, but Dr. Kush Bandi, who has been examined on behalf of the appellant categorically stated that the appellant's bone has been fixed and now he is able to perform his routine work.
He can walk easily without any support.
There is no deformity in x-ray report (Ex.-42).
Appellant has not filed any document regarding permanent disability issued by the District Medical Board.

7. In view of the above, the below Tribunal has rightly considered the permanent disability only 3%,
therefore, the finding given by the claims Tribunal appears to be just and proper.

The appellant has filed bills of his treatment (Ex.- P/51 to P/103) and Tribunal has rightly considered all the relevant bills and awarded an mount of Rs.1,40,500/- towards compensation of medical expenditures, which has been duly calculated, therefore, there is no need to award any further amount in this head.

8. As per para 61 of the impugned award, it is quite clear that appellant was admitted in the hospital only for a period of five days, therefore, below Tribunal has rightly granted compensation of Rs.10,000/- in the head of transportation, attendant and special diet.
There is no material available on record to show that the appellant is required any further treatment.
Hence, he does not deserve for any further claim in the head of future treatment.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid, this Court is of the considered opinion that the impugned order passed by the below Tribunal is based upon cogent evidence available on record.
The findings given by the below Tribunal appears to be just and proper and claim amount is adequate, therefore, no interference is required.
Accordingly, the appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
Both the parties shall bear their own expenses.
